hints: Notice the table varies both direction - away from observer versus towards observer - and speed from $5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Recall the Doppler rule for sound: moving away stretches the observed wavelength and lowers $f_o$, while moving towards compresses it and raises $f_o$.
Compare the two away cases: the faster recession stretches each successive wavefront further apart, so decide which of $5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ away gives the longer wavelength.
walkthrough: Identify the set-up: constant source frequency, stationary observer, and source speeds of $5$, $10$, $15$ and $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ either away or towards.

State the Doppler cause-and-effect: observed wavelength $\lambda_o$ is increased when the source moves away and decreased when it moves towards, with observed frequency $f_o = v/\lambda_o$ where $v$ is sound speed.
So both away options A and B must give $f_o$ below the source frequency, while both towards options C and D must give $f_o$ above it. The smallest $f_o$ must be an away motion.
For recession, a larger source speed $v_s$ adds more distance between successive wavefronts, so $\lambda_o$ is larger for $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ away than for $5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ away.
Larger $\lambda_o$ means smaller $f_o$, so $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ away gives a smaller observed frequency than $5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ away. This is option B.

options.A: Moving away lowers the observed frequency, but $5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ gives a smaller wavelength stretch and so a higher frequency than moving away faster.
options.B: Moving away at the larger $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ gives the longest observed wavelength and therefore the smallest observed frequency $f_o = v/\lambda_o$.
options.C: Moving towards the observer compresses the waves, giving a shorter observed wavelength and a higher observed frequency.
options.D: Moving towards at $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ gives the greatest compression and so the largest observed frequency, not the smallest.
